ctx.x: were nice and clean but there was nobody up there but me so I stayed up there two weeks and I got frightened and I didn't know what that house was doing. They were snatching people up what it's for; and taking care of business and that's so I stayed two weeks and I left, then I went down on 32nd Street and asked the lady for a room, but I smelled the very pungent odor and that odor it was too much, incense and I think it was opium that I was smelling, and she looked like she had this makeup on, yes, young man, I…

So I started living on Edgecombe Avenue) and I was living right across the street from one of my aunts and didn't know it. She didn't know it either, so now I'm here in this big city as you said, and I'm seeing lights and guys are going through the Tree of Hope and I'm meeting these big stars. I was going to a place called the Rhythm Club, Jelly Roll Morton, Fletcher Henderson, Coleman Hawkins, and Elmer Williams, and Rex Stewart -- by the way, he's from Washington and I'm meeting these and Ovie Alston and Sandy…

read music. Yes, sir. Where you come from anyway (unintelligible) no, sir, I come from Lafayette, Louisiana. Can you read music. Yes, sir, well, go and get it. This is 12 o'clock in the day. I got my tuxedo and put it on. Read that. I read it.

items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Jelly Roll and some man there was named Al somebody... Jelly Roll opened up... I did just that. I stayed there and Jelly Roll Morton and he was

ctx.x: At the Rhythm Club in front of everybody. Read that. So I read it. He said, go home and take your tuxedo off and then come back at 8 o'clock here. Yes, sir.

I did it and so Jelly Roll and some man there was named Al somebody, wearing a big diamond ring, and Jelly Roll opened up, cursing the chick out, come up here you so and so: and sing a song, and don't you rush the tempo and you hear what I said, and she was crying. Get up there now and he started playing one of them gut bucket things--take that mute and put it in that half pocket and I did just that. I stayed there and Jelly Roll Morton and he was -- those poor women, was in awful shape and the gangsters come in,…

So then it seemed like overnight, seeing that thing happen like it happen -- something happen and wouldn't nobody come to work. Can't go over there now, little later, little later, then we went to work and some guys come in there and Jelly Roll Morton say come on, let's get behind the piano and then make it out the back door and that's what we did and then
